title: Certificates of Deposit: penalties dated in the grace period are outside the wrong-rate check
content:
## Scope

This rule applies when a Certificates of Deposit certificate's most recent early withdrawal penalty is being checked for a wrong rate or wrong penalty days. It removes from that check a penalty that sits on a grace-period withdrawal.

## Rule

A penalty whose posted date falls on day 1 through the last day of the tier's grace period, counted from the day after the certificate's maturity date, sits on a grace-period withdrawal and is outside the wrong-rate and wrong-days check. Such a penalty is reversed under the bank's policy for penalties charged on grace-period withdrawals.

## How the days are counted

- The anchor is the maturity date shown on the certificate.
- Day 1 is the day after the maturity date.
- The window runs through the day numbered with the tier's grace period length, both ends included.
- A penalty posted on the maturity date itself (day 0), or after the last grace day, is not caught by this rule.

## Boundary cases (illustrative grace length of 5 days, not a tier value)

Maturity date 10 June.

| Penalty posted on | Day count after the maturity date | Outside the wrong-rate check? |
|---|---|---|
| 10 June | 0 | No |
| 11 June | 1 | Yes |
| 15 June | 5 | Yes |
| 16 June | 6 | No |

## Points of judgement

**A penalty was posted during grace at a rate that also looks wrong. Is it handled under the wrong-rate check?**
No. Whatever else may be wrong with it, a penalty posted within the grace window sits on a grace-period withdrawal and is handled under the policy for penalties on grace-period withdrawals.
